journey.name: Memory Leak Check - Media Viewer Surface
journey.description:
Verifies that opening full-screen image and video media viewers, swiping through images, and dismissing the overlay does not leak image loaders, Coil targets, or ViewModels.
Executes 3 loop iterations with theme switches (dark/light) to trigger Activity recreation while observing LeakCanary output.
Bench note (2026-10-31): tapping a feed image opens the viewer with "This post has no images" because the bench fixtures can't resolve the post, so the image-verify step fails on bench until that fixture gap is fixed. The full-screen video player works on bench.

actions.action: Verify that the app is open on the Home feed
Tap a post image in the feed to open the full-screen media viewer
Verify that the image is displayed in full-screen media viewer overlay
Swipe left to view the next image if available
Swipe right to view the previous image
Tap the Close button or swipe down to dismiss the media viewer
Verify that the Home feed is visible
Scroll down to find a video post in the feed
Tap the video post player or thumbnail to open full-screen video player
Verify that the video player overlay is active
Press back or tap Close to dismiss the video player
Verify that the Home feed is visible
Switch the device to dark theme
Switch the device back to light theme
Repeat all of the steps above two more times
Press the Home button to send the app to the background, then wait 15 seconds for LeakCanary analysis
Verify that no LeakCanary leak notification appears except for known accessibility delegate semantics cache
